VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, not by reading. I stood up a real PostgreSQL 16 cluster, reconstructed a test baseline for the 7 touched tables from the archive DDL (including the archived validate_essay_tone_fields trigger), and applied the seed. Result: exact row counts as reported; three consecutive applies produced zero drift (essays 106, modules 49, sections 8, fsli 24, categories 1, settings 2, finance_sections 4 after each run).

FIDELITY PROVEN MECHANICALLY. A checker byte-compared the DB contents against the archive: 105/105 essay titles identical (including all 8 doubled apostrophes), 24/24 fsli_pages rows identical across all 8 columns, 8/8 sections rows identical. The 29 hardcoded module UUIDs in the three essay files map 1:1 onto the 29 non-fundamentals modules I seeded, each in the right track.

CATEGORY: chose the SUBQUERY approach as recommended. Seeded 'General'/'finance-general' with a generated UUID (section_id resolved from sections.slug), and every one of the 106 essays resolves category_id by subquery. Justification: it does not depend on the ALTER TABLE ... SET DEFAULT that 20260219_004 added and the fresh baseline may not carry; it carries no literal UUID; and it still works if the row already exists under a different id (e.g. created via the admin UI). Verified: 0 essays with NULL category_id.

MODULE ID RESOLUTION: module_id comes from (SELECT id FROM finance_modules WHERE track_slug = <track> AND sort_order = v.module_no), with module_no decoded from the slug prefix. No literal UUID appears anywhere in the file (verified by grep: zero UUID-shaped strings outside comments). Because a scalar subquery that matches nothing yields NULL *silently* rather than failing, I added assertions that would otherwise let a typo produce orphans.

ASSERTIONS ARE LOAD-BEARING AND TESTED. A negative test pre-planted a module at the wrong sort_order; the seed aborted with 'seed: 5 curriculum stubs have NULL module_id — module lookup failed' and rolled back completely (essays 0, sections 0, fsli 0 afterwards). So a broken reconstruction cannot leave half-seeded curriculum. Thresholds use >= where later admin rows could legitimately raise a count, and exact equality only for the closed sets this file owns.

PUBLISHED ESSAY BODY GOES IN essays.content, NOT content_json. src/pages/FinanceEssayPage.tsx reads essay.content and passes it through contentToHtml; ArticleBody parses it with parseTiptapJson. grep for content_json across src/ returns zero hits — the app never reads it. content is therefore seeded with a TipTap doc JSON string (validated as parseable JSON) and content_json is left NULL.

PUBLISHED ESSAY LEAVES voice_role NULL. The archived validate_essay_tone_fields() trigger RAISEs on publish when voice_role names a role whose *_fields JSONB is empty. With voice_role NULL no branch fires. Confirmed against the real trigger in the test DB: the row inserted with status='published' and voice_validated_at set, no exception.

PUBLISHED ESSAY HAS module_id NULL. Attaching it to a curriculum module would list a rebuild notice as that module's lesson 01.01, which is its own kind of dishonesty. open_risks: UNIQUE CONSTRAINT NAMES ARE INFERRED, NOT OBSERVED. The baseline schema file (20260731*_baseline_schema.sql, referenced by _archive/README.md) is not in the repo, so I derived every constraint from the archive DDL. The ON CONFLICT target columns are what matter and they are safe, but if the baseline made finance_modules unique on (track_slug, slug) instead of slug alone, or omitted the essays_slug_unique index, the corresponding ON CONFLICT clause will error at apply time. FIX IS ONE LINE PER STATEMENT — no data change. Worth a `\d public.essays` / `\d public.finance_modules` before the first apply.

The 105 stubs carry finance_section = NULL, exactly as the three source migrations left them. Curriculum navigation is unaffected (FinanceModulePage and useTrackEssayCounts key on module_id), but useFinanceSectionEssays filters on finance_section and will return nothing for these. I kept verbatim fidelity over app convenience; if the owner wants that legacy listing populated, one UPDATE joining finance_modules.track_slug fixes it and is a content decision, not a reconstruction one.

The 11 derived module slugs are my mechanical derivation, not production's. If production used different slugs, existing external links to /finance/<track>/<module> for those 11 will 404 (the 18 authored slugs are safe). Nothing internal breaks: essays resolve by module_id, and the App.tsx redirects only reference authored slugs.

planning module 07 'Capital Needs' -> growth-financing-planning is a content-based inference, the one match I would not call certain. If wrong, the effect is a wrong title/thesis on one module; the 3 essays under it still bind correctly because binding is on sort_order.

20260204074340's sections upsert uses DO UPDATE, which I preserved. On a re-run that overwrites any manifesto or name the owner has since edited through the admin UI. Same for finance_sections descriptions. This is intentional (both are structural taxonomy the source migration existed to force) but it is a real replay hazard worth knowing about; fsli_pages, finance_settings, finance_modules and essays are all DO NOTHING precisely to avoid it.

The published note's canonical URL depends on module_id being nullable and on FinanceEssayPage's slug-only lookup. If a future change scopes essay lookup by module, /finance/.../site-rebuild-note stops resolving. The row is still readable via PostgREST, so the anon-can-read-published acceptance check is unaffected.

My verification ran against a test baseline I reconstructed, not the real one. It proves the DML is valid, idempotent, self-consistent and verbatim; it does not prove the real baseline's RLS lets an anonymous role read the published row and not the drafts. That check belongs on the real DB: as anon, `select slug from essays where slug='site-rebuild-note'` must return 1 row and `where slug='sf-01-01'` must return 0.
